cards.title: Why the original Unix pipeline used a single vertical bar
cards.body: Doug McIlroy conceived Unix pipelines in 1964, proposing that programs act like garden hoses connected together. Ken Thompson finally implemented the feature overnight in 1973. Seeking a concise syntax, Thompson seized on the vertical bar character. It existed on Model 33 Teletype keyboards but was virtually unused by existing command-line programs, making it the perfect delimiter to stream output from one program directly into another without temporary files.

cards.title: The punch card column limit that still dictates code formatting
cards.body: Many modern style guides still urge programmers to limit lines of code to 80 characters. This arbitrary convention traces directly to 1928, when IBM introduced the standard 80-column rectangular-hole punch card. Decades later, early text terminals like the 1978 DEC VT100 adopted an 80-column text display to maintain backward compatibility with card readers, anchoring a mechanical manufacturing constraint from the 1920s permanently into modern software linters.

cards.title: The fast inverse square root constant that baffled id Software
cards.body: In 1999, id Software released Quake III Arena featuring a lightning-fast algorithm to compute the inverse square root needed for 3D physics vector calculations. Bypassing slow floating-point divisions, the code used an unheralded bit manipulation trick centered on the hex constant 0x5f3759df. Accompanied by the legendary code comment 'what the fuck?', the trick cut CPU cycles dramatically years before graphics chips supported dedicated hardware instructions.

cards.title: Why the very first webcam pointed at a Trojan Room coffee pot
cards.body: In 1991, researchers in the Computer Laboratory at the University of Cambridge grew tired of walking to the breakroom only to find an empty coffee pot. Quentin Stafford-Fraser and Paul Jardetzky set up a camera capturing a 128-by-128 greyscale frame of the pot every few seconds, serving it to desktop monitors over their local network. In 1993, when web browsers added image support, it went live online as history's first webcam.

cards.title: How a spreadsheet formula error altered global austerity policy
cards.body: In 2010, Harvard economists Carmen Reinhart and Kenneth Rogoff published an influential paper arguing that countries with public debt exceeding 90% of GDP experience negative economic growth. Politicians globally cited this figure to justify severe budget cuts. In 2013, University of Massachusetts Amherst graduate student Thomas Herndon replicated their Excel spreadsheet and found an accidental formula glitch: an average calculation omitted five key countries entirely, completely invalidating the dramatic 90% debt cliff claim.

quizzes.question: Why did Ken Thompson choose the vertical bar '|' for Unix pipelines in 1973?
options: It was virtually unused by existing programs on Teletype keyboards
It resembled a physical water pipe in early printer manuals
The ASCII standard had just reserved it exclusively for networking
It was the only non-alphanumeric key on his keyboard
quizzes.explanation: Thompson chose '|' because it was readily available on Model 33 Teletypes and had no conflicting prior usage in shell commands.

quizzes.question: What historical hardware standard inspired the modern 80-character line length limit?
options: IBM's 80-column punch card introduced in 1928
The width of an 8-inch magnetic floppy disk sector
The maximum printable characters on a standard typewriter line
The memory size of early 1970s microprocessors
quizzes.explanation: IBM introduced the 80-column punch card format in 1928, which later defined the standard width of terminal screens like the VT100.

quizzes.question: What made the Quake III fast inverse square root code famous among game developers?
options: An obscure magic hexadecimal constant (0x5f3759df)
It was written in pure machine code by artificial intelligence
It required zero bytes of random access memory
It replaced matrix multiplication with bitwise addition
quizzes.explanation: The algorithm relied on an enigmatic hex constant, 0x5f3759df, which allowed fast floating-point approximations via integer bit shifts.

quizzes.question: What was the original purpose of the world's first webcam in 1991?
options: To check if an office coffee pot was full or empty
To monitor a physics lab laser experiment
To provide security surveillance for a server rack
To live-stream weather conditions over Cambridge
quizzes.explanation: Researchers at Cambridge pointed a video camera at their breakroom coffee pot so colleagues could avoid walking over to an empty pot.

quizzes.question: What coding error did graduate student Thomas Herndon uncover in Reinhart and Rogoff's 2010 economic study?
options: An Excel formula omitted five entire countries from an average
A missing semi-colon caused the statistical model to loop
The spreadsheet converted percentages into decimal integers
A macro accidentally deleted data from all recession years
quizzes.explanation: Herndon discovered that an Excel AVERAGE formula range omitted five rows of country data, fundamentally distorting the paper's conclusions.

guesses.prompt: How many columns of data did IBM's 1928 punch card standard contain, shaping code line limits for a century?
guesses.explanation: IBM standardized on 80 columns in 1928, establishing the formatting width that programmers and terminal emulators still follow today.

guesses.prompt: At what threshold of debt-to-GDP did Reinhart and Rogoff claim economic growth abruptly collapses before an Excel error was found?
guesses.explanation: The paper claimed growth drops sharply once national debt exceeds 90% of GDP, a threshold widely cited before the spreadsheet bug was caught.

misconceptions.claim: Rigorous peer review guaranteed that Reinhart and Rogoff's landmark 2010 debt findings were mathematically sound.
misconceptions.explanation: The influential paper contained basic spreadsheet errors, including an Excel cell-selection glitch that excluded five countries from analysis.
